eyebrow: Brother, 2026-09-04, lane E90: the door costs 728 times the hand route on a one-line change
title: A light path for small changes, or an honest price
stamp: Written 2026-09-04 by lane E90 on branch wbs/e90-light-path-decision from hub/main d3f82368, after reading the t7 gauntlet report whole and measuring the engine's own cost on a throwaway git repository with the stub decomposer and stub worker (the DOOR_MODEL_CMD and MODEL_WORKER_CMD seam scripts/test_brother_run.py already uses), three runs per configuration. No engine file was changed by this lane. Ruled A, by the delegate under the founder's 2026-09-10 order; see the decided block below.
question: An external evaluator asked the door for a one-line edit plus a one-line test. By hand it took 0.78 seconds. Through the door it took 568.03 seconds, about 728 times, of which 147 seconds was decomposition before any unit was claimed. The proof half of the bar held: the receipt re-ran the test with the dependency reverted and showed it fails without the change. Does the door get a light single-unit path when the outcome names one file and one check, does it keep its shape and say the price out loud before the wait, or does it change nothing and let the cost block carry the overhead after the fact?
plain_summary: Measured here, on a toy repository with the model calls stubbed out, a whole two-unit run costs the engine 2.58 seconds and a one-unit run 1.69 seconds. So of the evaluator's 568 seconds, at most about 3 were Brother's own code and roughly 565 were two headless model sessions waiting to answer. That changes what the three options are really worth. Option A skips the decomposer call for a one-file one-check outcome, which removes the measured 147 second planning leg and leaves about 421 seconds, still 540 times the hand route, and it removes the one thing the evaluator said would bring him back, because a single unit has no dependency to revert. Option B changes no code path: it puts a plain line on the front page saying the door is not for a one-line edit, and it puts the size of the wait on the intent screen before the wait starts, at the seam that already prints what earlier runs really took. Option C leaves everything alone and relies on the cost block, which is honest but arrives after the person has already waited.

recommendation_why: Because of what the measurement says the overhead actually is. On a throwaway repository with both model calls stubbed, a full two-unit run cost the engine a median 2.58 seconds and a one-unit run 1.69 seconds, both exit 0, three runs each. So of the evaluator's 568.03 seconds, at most about 3 were Brother's own code and roughly 565 were two headless model sessions. A light path therefore cannot buy engine time, because there is none to buy; it can only remove a model call. Removing the planning call buys the 147 seconds t7 measured and leaves about 421, roughly 540 times the hand route against a bar of 1.5 times, so option A shortens the wait without ever approaching the target, and it does so by deleting the dependency-revert re-run that was the single reason the evaluator said he would come back. The worker leg it cannot touch was 418.5 seconds for two units that ran concurrently, and the report gives no per-unit worker duration, so how much of that a single unit would still cost is NO-DATA. Given that, the useful move is the one that costs nothing and fixes the actual complaint: say before the wait what the wait is, on the front page and on the screen that already reports what earlier runs really took. B keeps the proof half that passed, concedes the half that cannot be won today, and leaves A buildable the moment the missing measurement makes it worth building.
flip: Flip to A if a single headless worker session for one trivial unit is measured at under about 60 seconds, which nobody has measured (the t7 report gives 418.5 seconds for two concurrent sessions and nothing per unit). At that figure the 147 second planning leg becomes the majority of the wait, so removing it changes the experience rather than trimming it, and the LOVE moment can be kept by restricting the light path to outcomes that genuinely have no second unit to depend on. Flip to C if the founder decides the small-change case is not one Brother wants at all, in which case a limit on the front page is an apology for a case that was never in scope and the cost block is enough.
ruling: A. Chosen by the delegate under the founder's order of 2026-09-10 ("fable make the best decision instead of me and close this seamlessly for tomorrow's cut"). The shipped tree already runs option A: FAST-0 (scripts/brother_run.py, fast_route_eligibility, called unconditionally at lines 5171 and 5179-5180 whenever no --plan is given and the run is not a resume) skips the decomposer session for an outcome that already names an existing file and an existing check in the narrow shape it recognizes, matching option A's own description. Option B's mechanism (the price paragraph, build_price_block) was also built and also ships, additively, but does not replace the engine change option A describes. See the decided block below for the full evidence and the flip condition.
